subject.title: Bug: Telegram delivery queue recovery can replay old sendMessage replies and duplicate delivery-mirror transcript entries

question: How should OpenClaw handle legacy pending Telegram delivery-queue rows that have ambiguous sendMessage failure evidence but no persisted recovery state?
rationale: Source inspection shows current main can distinguish new ambiguous rows, but older JSON entries predate that state; choosing quarantine, pending deferral, or replay requires a human tradeoff between duplicate delivery and dropping unsent messages.

options.title: Quarantine Ambiguous Legacy Telegram Rows
options.body: Doctor or migration would move old Telegram rows with ambiguous network/sendMessage errors out of pending recovery and preserve diagnostics, avoiding duplicate delivery at the cost of possible unsent replies.

options.title: Keep Recoverable Pending Semantics
options.body: Legacy rows would remain pending for future reconciliation or operator tooling, but maintainers must accept that some old rows may stay stranded until a surfaced repair path exists.

options.title: Replay Legacy Rows
options.body: OpenClaw would continue recovering old rows as send intents, preserving delivery attempts but accepting the duplicate-send risk this issue reports.

recommendation.title: Quarantine Ambiguous Legacy Telegram Rows
recommendation.body: Doctor or migration would move old Telegram rows with ambiguous network/sendMessage errors out of pending recovery and preserve diagnostics, avoiding duplicate delivery at the cost of possible unsent replies.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent maintainer-signal history around outbound recovery semantics and message-delivery safety decisions.
